title: Cancer: current or history, and metastases
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's cancer as documented at this visit.
note:
Chief Complaint
Pain in the lower back and hips.

HPI
The patient is an 81-year-old man presenting for evaluation of persistent skeletal discomfort. He has a history of prostate cancer that was surgically removed and treated several years ago. He reports that the primary site remains clear, and there is no evidence of local recurrence at the original site. However, he is currently experiencing aching pain in his spine and pelvis. He describes the discomfort as a dull, constant ache that worsens with weight-bearing activities. He denies any new neurological deficits or changes in bowel or bladder function.

Medication List
Acetaminophen 650mg every 6 hours as needed for pain.

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented. He appears in no acute distress but demonstrates a guarded posture. Physical examination reveals tenderness upon palpation of the lumbar spine and bilateral hips. Range of motion is limited by discomfort. Neurological exam is intact with normal strength and sensation in all extremities.

Assessment
1. Prostate cancer with bone metastases. The primary carcinoma is stable and well-controlled. The current focus is the management of pain related to skeletal involvement.

Plan
1. Continue current pain management with acetaminophen.
2. Order a follow-up imaging study to evaluate the extent of the bone metastasis.
3. Provide education on non-pharmacological pain relief strategies.

Electronically signed, J. Lindqvist, PA-C, 05/14/2026
explanations: The prostate cancer was excised or eradicated, no treatment is directed to it and there is no evidence of it: personal history Z85.46 (no HCC). Any metastasis is still coded as a current secondary malignancy.
Bone metastases: C79.51, secondary malignant neoplasm of bone (HCC 18, which outranks the primary-site HCC).

distractors.why: Treatment ended and there is no evidence of the primary: code personal history (Z85), not active cancer.
Metastasis is coded as a secondary malignancy, even when the primary is history.
The metastases are in bone, not the liver.

hccs.label: Cancer Metastatic to Bone/Other and Unspecified Metastatic Cancer; Acute Leukemia Except Myeloid
